title: Temperature, Humidity, VPD and Plant Water Exchange
summary: Vapor pressure deficit is a combined temperature-humidity relationship that helps describe atmospheric drying demand, but plant water exchange also depends on leaf temperature, stomata, roots, light and airflow.

sections.title: VPD combines temperature and humidity
sections.body: Relative humidity cannot be interpreted independently of temperature because saturation vapor pressure changes strongly with temperature. VPD expresses the difference between saturation and actual vapor pressure and therefore gives a more physically meaningful view of atmospheric vapor demand than RH alone.

sections.title: Leaf conditions can differ from room air
sections.body: Radiation, airflow, transpiration and boundary layers can make leaf temperature differ from the air sensor reading. Leaf-to-air vapor relationships therefore require representative measurement and should not be reduced to a universal room target for every cultivar and crop stage.

sections.title: Water demand links atmosphere and root zone
sections.body: As atmospheric demand, light and plant size change, water movement through the plant and root-zone depletion can change as well. Irrigation scheduling is therefore connected to environmental conditions rather than being a completely independent clock-based practice.
